children: lost nearly 40% in premarket trading on Tuesday after announcing that its lead candidate, rademikibart, failed to reach the primary endpoint in a Phase 2 trial for patients with asthma.

The global trial, designed to evaluate rademikibart as an add-on therapy for acute exacerbations in adults and adolescents with asthma and type 2 inflammation, had treatment failure as its primary endpoint.
While the injectable cut the treatment failure rate by roughly 66% over 28 days compared to placebo, the effect was not statistically significant, Connect Biopharma
said, citing topline data from the 160-subject study named Seabreeze STAT Asthma.

However, the company noted a statistically significant improvement in a key secondary endpoint called the absolute one-week change in post-bronchodilator (post-BD) forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1), which it has selected as a proposed primary endpoint in Phase 3.
The experimental therapy was well tolerated with no new safety signals, the San Diego, California-based biopharma added.

Topline data from its Phase 2 Seabreeze STAT COPD study in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is expected later this month, after which the company plans to meet with the FDA to discuss late-stage trial

title: Connect Biopharma drops as asthma candidate fails in mid-stage trial
